context: The integer n is positive. The figure shows the tree constructed and retained by build_tree. Each circle represents a node that takes constant space. Arrows connect a parent to its left and right children. A brace on the right is labeled “n levels.”
description: The figure shows the first three levels. Eight arrows extend from the four nodes at level 3 to ellipses, indicating further expansion. The right column, “Nodes per level,” lists 2⁰, 2¹, 2², …, 2ⁿ⁻¹. The table adds the level numbers, the decimal values of the first few terms, and a reading of the final power.

frames.explanation: At the bottom, the level counts add up to 2⁰ + 2¹ + 2² + … + 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 2ⁿ − 1, or two to the power n, minus one. Left and right pointers keep the new nodes attached to the tree after the calls that created them return. All these nodes therefore occupy memory at the same time. Although the call stack has only O(n) depth, the whole tree requires O(2ⁿ) space. The arrow at the bottom points to this conclusion.
frames.title: Space needed to store a perfect binary tree with n levels

summary: To find the space needed for an entire perfect binary tree with n levels, count all the nodes retained in memory as well as the recursive call stack.
